title: AIC Criminology Research Fund 2026
description:
The Commonwealth as represented by the Australian Institute of Criminology (AIC) is seeking sumissions for the Criminology Research Fund 2026.
The Criminology Research Fund (CRF) program is a competitive program that provides funds to support the conduct of high quality, policy-relevant research projects in the area of crime and criminal justice. The CRF is funded through annual contributions by the Commonwealth, State and Territory Governments.
The CRF program is administered by the AIC on the basis of recommendations from the Criminology Research Advisory Council (Advisory Council). The Advisory Council, which includes representatives from each of the contributing Governments, provides recommendations to the Director of the AIC on research priorities and an assessment of applications made under the annual CRF program. The Advisory Council bases its assessment on the recommendations of an Academic Panel chaired by the Academic Advisor (an AIC research staff member).
The AIC will award contracts in varying values.

publicQuestions.question:
Will the Principle consider or allow the following:

1.The submission of an alternate or accompanying format price file, for the following reasons:

 a) The Items requested in the price file are quite generalised and will potentially limit the principles’ ability to choose the most appropriate product available, or limit the supplier’s

ability to recommend the most suitable product

b) By allowing alternate or accompanying price/product files, more options will be available to the principle, increasing the ability to achieve a desired result

c) By allowing an alternate format, suppliers will likely be able to update the principle on price variations in a more detailed manner

2. Quarterly updates to product/price files, for the following reasons:

a) Many specified products will fall under agency platforms, meaning price changes and timings will be dictated to by the product suppliers and not the tender suppliers

b) Volatility in fertiliser pricing on the back of the middle east conflict

c) By allowing more regular price reviews, suppliers will be able to ensure best value is being provided to the Principle and will ensure price files are maintained accurately, which is important from an invoicing point of view, and matching the principles PO’s
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Tenderer,

Thank you for your enquiry regarding SSROC T2026-02 Supply and Delivery of Agricultural Products Services Tender.

In response to your specific questions:

1.	The RFT already contemplates this scenario. Tenderers are reminded of the following provisions that remain in effect:

The Pricing Schedule (Form 7) contained within Part 3-2 Mandatory Returnable Schedules must be completed in full using the prescribed Excel format. The RFT expressly states that “Tenderers must not alter the contents or formatting of the Pricing Schedule, other than to include additional line items where relevant or referred to in the pricing table.” Accordingly, the prescribed Form 7 remains a mandatory conforming requirement and cannot be omitted or replaced.

At the same time, the RFT expressly encourages innovation, stating that “Tenderers are encouraged to submit innovative or alternative ways of servicing this contract.” An alternate or supplementary product/price file may be submitted, provided that:

a.	A fully compliant and conforming Tender, including a completed Form 7, is submitted in the first instance.

b.	The alternate or supplementary file is submitted through Form 22 (Summary of Alternative Tenders) as an alternative or supplementary submission and is clearly identified as such.

c.	The supplementary file is cross-referenced to the relevant line items contained in Form 7.

d.	The alternate file does not replace or contradict the conforming schedule and may only be submitted as a supplement to it.

Tenderers are also reminded that the basket of goods contained in Form 7 is recognised within the RFT as a generic and representative basket only and is not intended to encompass all products that may be procured under the Agreement. Councils may engage Preferred Suppliers for items outside the basket through the SSROC Vendor Panel at the rates and conditions agreed under the PSMA.

2. This matter is governed by the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement (PSMA).

The RFT states that "the Agreement Terms and conditions of pricing, price variations and replacement costs are stipulated in the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement (PSMA)" (Part 4 of the RFT). Tenderers are directed to review the draft PSMA in full.

The formal contract review mechanism includes an Annual Contract Review Report, which encompasses pricing review and market benchmarking as standard components. This represents the primary structured mechanism for price file updates under the Agreement.

Tenderers wishing to propose departures from the pricing variation provisions of the draft PSMA — including any proposal for more frequent (e.g. quarterly) price reviews — are invited to do so via Form 6 (Proposed Contract Departures) in the Part 3-1 Returnable Schedules. Any such departure will be considered by SSROC on its merits and may be subject to negotiation following evaluation. Proposed departures will not render a tender non-conforming, but the Principal reserves the right to accept, reject, or negotiate any proposed departure.

Tenderers proposing a quarterly mechanism are encouraged to include in their Form 6 submission the specific categories or product lines for which the departure is sought, the proposed triggering criteria, and any suggested guardrails (e.g. CPI or index caps, notice periods), to facilitate the Principal's assessment.

Should you require any further clarification, please submit your questions through the tender portal in accordance with the tender process and timelines outlined in the tender documentation.

We thank you for your interest in this opportunity and look forward to receiving your submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1 - Can you provide more detailed usage information for each site so transport and volumes can be better understood and considered in our offer.

Q2 - With delivery to a campus where multiple areas are using the linen service is it expected that the provider deliver to each user area or will delivery be to one central point at the campus and collected from this staging area by users

Q3 - Can you clarify what contract term you are seeking to implement with successful provider eg 1 2 or 3 years
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Can you provide more detailed usage information for each site so transport and volumes can be better understood and considered in our offer?

Response:

TAFE Queensland has provided the best available information to support suppliers in preparing their offers. The volumes included within the procurement documentation are indicative only and have been developed for evaluation purposes.

Please refer to Attachment A – Specification and Attachment C – Linen Hire & Laundry Pricing List (Pricing Scenario tab) for indicative demand information.

As outlined in the Specification, service demand varies by campus and is influenced by factors such as student enrolments, training schedules, practical class delivery, events, facility utilisation, and seasonal activity. Accordingly, TAFE Queensland is unable to provide guaranteed site-specific usage volumes. Suppliers should base their offers on their capacity to service nominated locations and accommodate fluctuations in demand throughout the contract term.

The current estimated demand across the TAFE Queensland network is approximately 2,750 to 4,300 items per week; however, actual volumes may be higher or lower depending on operational requirements.

Q2. With delivery to a campus where multiple areas are using the linen service, is it expected that the provider deliver to each user area or will delivery be to one central point at the campus and collected from this staging area by users?

Response:

For the purposes of tender evaluation, suppliers should assume that delivery and collection will occur at a single nominated delivery point within each campus.

Specific delivery arrangements may vary between campuses and service areas and will be confirmed during implementation with the successful supplier(s). Suppliers may identify any assumptions, site requirements, or alternative service delivery approaches within their offer submission.

Q3. Can you clarify what contract term you are seeking to implement with the successful provider, e.g. 1, 2 or 3 years?

Response:

The contract term is stated in both the Invitation to Offer and Attachment A – Specification. The proposed Standing Offer Arrangement term is three (3) years, with an option for TAFE Queensland to extend the arrangement by up to two (2) additional periods of twelve (12) months each, at TAFE Queensland's discretion. The maximum potential term is therefore five (5) years.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

In Part D – Schedule of Prices under “Termite Treatment”, it asks for confirmation that employee(s) hold a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical and a QBCC Termite Management – Physical licence. However, the services listed only require a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical licence.

Could you please confirm whether both licences are required, or only Chemical licensing for this tender?
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 13/Aug/2026 10:58 AM)

Thank you for your enquiry.

Tenderers are required to hold both a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical licence and a QBCC Termite Management – Physical licence.

While the termite treatment services currently listed in the Schedule of Rates primarily require a Termite Management – Chemical licence, the contract may include other termite management works that require a Termite Management – Physical licence. As subcontracting is not permitted under this arrangement, suppliers must be appropriately licensed to undertake the full range of potential termite-related services that may arise during the contract term.

Accordingly, the requirement for both licence types remains unchanged, and tenderers should ensure they can demonstrate compliance with both licensing requirements in their submission.

Please also note.

The QBCC Termite Management - Physical licence (along with the QBCC Termite Management – Chemical Licence) is only required if offering for the termite treatments, which is optional under this trade. The mandatory requirement for this SOA is the Pest Management Licence issued by Qld Health, which is required to undertake the basic and additional treatments etc.

title: TEN/2893 Waste Facilities Maintenance
description:
Council is inviting submissions from suitably qualified and experienced Suppliers for the provision of mechanical, hydraulic and associated maintenance services for Council's Waste Management and Resource Recovery Facilities.

The majority of works will be undertaken at the Bundaberg Materials Recovery Facility and Bundaberg Waste Management Facility located on University Drive, Bundaberg. The successful Supplier will also be required to provide maintenance, repairs and breakdown support across Council's landfill and transfer station network as required.

The Contract includes both scheduled preventative maintenance and reactive maintenance services. Key responsibilities will include the maintenance and repair of critical assets such as the MRF trommel, conveyor systems, balers, hydraulic equipment, motors, gearboxes, hydraulic tip wells, transfer station hydraulic gates and other operational plant and equipment. description:
